questions.q: What does using the marketing concept mean?
options: Creating the product after market research identifies customers' needs and wants
Selling at the lowest possible price
questions.explain: Customer needs come first; the product follows.
questions.evidence: using the marketing concept means the product is created after market research is used to identify the needs and wants of the customers.

questions.q: Why does a company identify a target market?
options: To focus marketing efforts on those most likely to buy
questions.explain: Targeting makes the marketing mix fit a specific group.
questions.evidence: Identifying a target market helps a company focus its marketing efforts on those who are most likely to buy its products or services.

questions.q: How should the strategies for the elements of the marketing mix relate to each other?
options: A strategy is built for each element and all are blended together
Each department designs its element independently
questions.explain: Product, place, promotion, price and people must work as one plan.
questions.evidence: A strategy must be constructed for each of the 5Ps, and all strategies must be blended with the strategies of the other elements.

questions.q: What is promotion almost always used for?
options: Getting people to try a new product, or non-users to try an existing one
questions.explain: Coupons and trial sizes are classic tactics to encourage trial.
questions.evidence: Promotion is almost always used to get people to try a new product or to get nonusers to try an existing product.

questions.q: What is publicity?
options: Information about a company or product in the news media that the company does not directly pay for
questions.explain: Publicity is part of public relations within the promotional mix.
questions.evidence: information about a company or product that appears in the news media and is not directly paid for by the company.

questions.q: What is Googlebot?
options: The program that fetches web pages — a crawler
questions.explain: Crawlers explore the web to find pages to add to the search index.
questions.evidence: The program that does the fetching is called Googlebot (also known as a crawler, robot, bot, or spider).

questions.q: What is SEO about?
options: Helping search engines understand your content and helping users find your site and decide to visit
Buying the top position in search results
Hiding text that only search engines can read
Making your site load more slowly for bots
questions.explain: Good SEO serves people first; search engines are one of your users.
questions.evidence: SEO—short for search engine optimization—is about helping search engines understand your content, and helping users find your site and make a decision about whether they should visit your site through a search engine.

questions.q: What is link text (anchor text)?
options: The URL hidden behind a link
The visible text part of a link
The title of a web page
questions.explain: Descriptive link text tells users and search engines what the target page is about.
questions.evidence: Link text (also known as anchor text ) is the text part of a link that you can see.

questions.q: Why should you avoid keyword stuffing?
options: It is tiring for users and against Google's spam policies
Search engines ignore repeated words anyway
It only works for paid ads
questions.explain: Write naturally; varied wording already covers more keywords.
questions.evidence: keyword stuffing is against Google's spam policies

questions.q: According to the GOV.UK guidance, what should you always combine your metrics with?
options: User research, improving the service based on insight from both
questions.explain: Numbers show what is happening; research shows why.
questions.evidence: You should always combine your metrics with user research and iterate your service based on insight from both to make sure it’s always improving.

questions.q: What is a service's 'digital take-up'?
options: The proportion of users who choose the digital service
The number of pages on the website
The cost of each online transaction
The time it takes to load the home page
questions.explain: Increasing take-up doesn't mean forcing everyone online — some users will need support.
questions.evidence: The proportion of users choosing the digital service is known as the service’s ‘digital take up’.

questions.q: What is environmental scanning?
options: A team continually collecting and evaluating information about the market environment
questions.explain: It looks at competitors, economy, technology, politics and society.
questions.evidence: many organizations assemble a team of specialists to continually collect and evaluate environmental information, a process called environmental scanning

questions.q: What is the goal of gathering environmental data?
options: To identify current and future market opportunities and threats
questions.explain: Opportunities and threats then shape the marketing strategy.
questions.evidence: The goal in gathering the environmental data is to identify current and future market opportunities and threats.

questions.q: Which components make up promotion?
options: Advertising, sales promotion, PR, personal selling, social media and e-commerce
questions.explain: Promotion is one element of the marketing mix.
questions.evidence: traditional advertising, sales promotion, public relations, personal selling, social media, and e-commerce

questions.q: What happens to an excellent product with excellent distribution but the wrong price?
options: It is still doomed to failure
Price never matters for good products
questions.explain: All elements of the marketing mix must be balanced.
questions.evidence: An excellent product with an excellent distribution system but an inappropriate price is also doomed to failure.

questions.q: For some products, especially services, what can a price that is too low do?
questions.explain: A very low price can signal poor quality.
questions.evidence: For some products (especially service products), having a price that is too low may actually hurt sales.

questions.q: Which kinds of factors affect consumer decision-making?
options: Cultural, social, individual and psychological factors
questions.explain: Marketers study each kind to understand buying decisions.
questions.evidence: These decision-making processes are affected by cultural, social, individual, and psychological factors.

questions.q: What are a person's reference groups?
options: The formal and informal groups that influence their buying behaviour
questions.explain: Examples include a club, a sorority or the people you work with.
questions.evidence: All the formal and informal groups that influence the buying behavior of an individual are considered that person

questions.q: What are the five basic forms of consumer market segmentation?
options: Price, product, place, promotion and people
Demographic, geographic, psychographic, benefit and volume
Local, regional, national, global and online
Age, gender, income, education and religion
questions.explain: Segmentation divides a market into groups with similar needs.
questions.evidence: The five basic forms of consumer market segmentation are demographic, geographic, psychographic, benefit, and volume.

questions.q: Why is demographic segmentation the most common form?
options: Demographic information is easy to obtain
It reveals the most about consumers
It is the only accurate form
questions.explain: Easy data doesn't always reveal the most about consumers.
questions.evidence: This form of market segmentation is the most common because demographic information is easy to obtain.

questions.q: How does purchase volume differ between business and consumer markets?
options: Businesses only buy once a year
Business customers buy in much larger quantities
questions.explain: B2B markets also have fewer, more concentrated buyers.
questions.evidence: Business customers buy in much larger quantities than consumers.

questions.q: What is geographic segmentation?
options: Segmenting by how much people buy
Segmenting by region, city size, market density or climate
Segmenting by the benefits people seek
questions.explain: Needs often differ between places, such as warm and cold climates.
questions.evidence: Geographic segmentation means segmenting markets by region of the country, city or county size, market density, or climate.

questions.q: Which tactics are common for tempting people to try a product?
questions.explain: Trial is one of the main goals of promotion.
questions.evidence: Coupons and trial-size containers of products are also common tactics used to tempt people to try a product.

questions.q: Why do consumer watchdogs applaud the informative function of promotion?
options: It helps consumers make more intelligent purchase decisions
questions.explain: Information about features and prices helps buyers compare.
questions.evidence: Consumer watchdogs and social critics applaud the informative function of promotion because it helps consumers make more intelligent purchase decisions.

questions.q: How can firms use promotion to keep customers loyal?
options: By raising prices for loyal customers
By stopping communication after a sale
By telling them when a product or service is improved
questions.explain: Promotion also aims to stop customers switching brands.
questions.evidence: Firms can also help keep customers loyal by telling them when a product or service is improved.

questions.q: What is traditional advertising?
options: Any paid, non-personal presentation by an identified sponsor
questions.explain: Paid and identified are what separate advertising from publicity.
questions.evidence: Traditional advertising is any paid form of nonpersonal presentation by an identified sponsor.

questions.q: What are advertising media?
options: The channels that carry advertising to prospective customers
questions.explain: Examples include TV, radio, print and online channels.
questions.evidence: The channels through which advertising is carried to prospective customers are the advertising media.

questions.q: What is public relations?
options: Any communication or activity designed to win goodwill or prestige
questions.explain: Publicity in the news media is one part of PR.
questions.evidence: Public relations is any communication or activity designed to win goodwill or prestige for a company or person.

questions.q: When has a marketer successfully created a buzz?
options: When one person tells one friend
When an ad runs once on TV
When a press release is published
When information spreads in a matrix and everyone is talking about the topic
questions.explain: Word of mouth is linear; buzz spreads in many directions at once.
questions.evidence: A marketer has successfully created a buzz when the interactions are so intense that the information moves in a matrix pattern rather than a linear one and everyone is talking about the topic.

questions.q: What is the title link in a Google search result?
options: The paid ad above the results
The headline of the result, which helps people decide which result to click
questions.explain: You can influence it through your page's title.
questions.evidence: The title link is the headline part of the search result and it can help people decide which search result to click.

questions.q: What does Google advise about advertisements on your pages?
options: Don't let them distract users or stop them reading your content
questions.explain: Ads are fine; overwhelming them is not.
questions.evidence: don't let them become overly distracting or prevent your users from reading your content

questions.q: What does it suggest if your content is mainly made to attract visits from search engines?
options: It's a warning sign to rethink how you create content
That your SEO is working perfectly
That you should add more keywords
That Google will rank it first
questions.explain: Google rewards helpful, people-first content.
questions.evidence: is a warning sign that you should reevaluate how you're creating content

questions.q: Does Google have a preferred word count for content?
options: No — writing to a word count for Google is a warning sign
questions.explain: Write as much as the topic and audience need.
questions.evidence: Are you writing to a particular word count because you've heard or read that Google has a preferred word count?

questions.q: Will adding or removing lots of content just to make a site seem 'fresh' improve rankings?
options: Yes, freshness is the top ranking factor
questions.explain: Changes should serve readers, not imagined ranking rules.
questions.evidence: (No, it won't)

questions.q: Why self-assess your content against Google's questions?
options: To gauge whether it is helpful and reliable
questions.explain: The questions focus on value for readers.
questions.evidence: Evaluating your own content against these questions can help you gauge if the content you're making is helpful and reliable.

questions.q: How many mandatory KPIs must a GOV.UK service collect and publish data for?
questions.explain: They are cost per transaction, user satisfaction, completion rate and digital take-up.
questions.evidence: You must collect and publish data for the 4 mandatory key performance indicators

questions.q: When designing metrics, what should you try to sum up in a single line?
questions.explain: Metrics only make sense against the service's purpose.
questions.evidence: Aim to sum up why your service exists in a single line.

questions.q: What should you check before deciding to use an analytics tool?
options: Whether it is the most expensive
Whether it has the most features
questions.explain: There are many commercial and free open-source options.
questions.evidence: You should check whether a tool meets your needs before you decide to use it.

questions.q: Where can government teams find and compare analytics suppliers?
questions.explain: Searching for analytics tool comparisons also helps.
questions.evidence: You can also find and compare suppliers on the Digital Marketplace

questions.q: What is a service's completion rate?
options: Digital transactions completed as a percentage of those started
Visitors who view the home page
questions.explain: A low completion rate shows where users drop out.
questions.evidence: is the number of digital transactions that your users complete as a percentage of all digital transactions that your users start

questions.q: When is an 'Apply for a patent' transaction considered complete?
options: Only when the patent is granted
When the user opens the form
When the user submits the application, whether or not it succeeds
questions.explain: Completion measures the transaction, not its outcome.
questions.evidence: the Apply for a patent transaction is considered complete when the user has submitted an application, regardless of whether the application is successful

questions.q: Do transactions completed with assisted digital support count in the completion rate?
questions.explain: Assisted digital users still use the digital service.
questions.evidence: This includes transactions where the user receives support from someone to use the digital service
